clue.text: Singer born in grand Merseyside town

parts.note: b. is the standard abbreviation for born in biographies
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
Crosby is a town on the coast of Merseyside, north of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A singer was born in a grand town on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here: it supplies its own letters. Merseyside is the county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was the hugely popular American crooner of 'White Christmas', an example of a singer.

clue.text: Barrister forgoing fine cheese

indicators.note: forgoing means doing without, so the letter for fine is dropped from the barrister word

parts.note: a brief is informal for a barrister, the lawyer one briefs
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns down some fine cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister is a court lawyer, and 'my brief' is slang for one's lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's-milk cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: One dubious name for a volatile gas

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or shady, so the letters of the word one are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone gives a questionable name to an unstable gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' rearranges ONE to EON, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, and as a gas it evaporates and disperses readily, the chemist's sense of volatile.

clue.text: They may be running moment race is off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of moment race is are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the race has just been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports broadcasters give a running commentary, a continuous description as events happen, so these may be running.

clue.text: Poet from Brentwood is talented

indicators.note: from tells us to take letters out of the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: A poet from the Essex town of Brentwood is gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Brentwood is a town in Essex, England; the letters run across its end into the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist writes odes, lyric verses addressed to a subject, so is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Decorative item from Paris bent, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of Paris bent are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ornament from Paris got bent, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastpin is a brooch worn on the chest, a piece of ornamental jewellery.

clue.text: Almost bald celebrity

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut from the word for bald

parts.note: stark means bare or blunt, as in a bald or stark statement

explanation.surface: A famous person who is nearly bald.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a synonym for a celebrity.

clue.text: Appropriate steps taken at the Christmas dinner dance?

definitions.text: Appropriate steps taken at the Christmas dinner dance?

parts.words: Appropriate steps taken at the Christmas dinner dance?
parts.note: the festive roast bird plus a brisk walk would be fitting steps at a Christmas meal, and the combination names a ragtime dance

explanation.surface: What moves suit a dance held at the Christmas dinner?
explanation.walkthrough: The roast bird traditional at a British Christmas dinner joins a word for quick steps, giving the name of a ragtime dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot was a lively ragtime ballroom dance popular around 1910.

clue.text: Appropriate lament, we hear, for a hunted creature at sea

parts.note: right means fitting or appropriate

indicators.note: we hear signals the word for lament is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a wail is a cry of lament

explanation.surface: A fitting lament for an animal hunted at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The right whale was so named as the 'right' one to hunt, and was pursued almost to extinction by whalers.

clue.text: Group from golf club, by first

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
maiden means first, as in a maiden voyage or speech

explanation.surface: A club of golfers stands next to the first of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden is a British heavy-metal band, a musical group.

clue.text: Boast in British newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A boast appears in a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to talk boastfully, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Part of motorway difficult to bear

parts.note: hard means difficult
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: A section of motorway is hard to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the emergency lane along the edge of a motorway is called by this name; Americans would say the shoulder.

clue.text: Collection of books to be found in mate's tent, by implication?

parts.note: these letters are a fresh arrangement of the word for a will, so a new form of that word describes them

explanation.surface: A set of books turns up in a friend's tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: NEW signals an anagram of TESTAMENT, and that anagram is MATESTENT, the clue's 'mate's tent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The second part of the Christian Bible is a collection of twenty-seven books.

clue.text: Fish as it thawed out

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters of as it thawed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frozen fish thaws out.
explanation.definitionFit: The twaite shad is a herring-like European fish that swims up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: Style of jazz, most important, and current

parts.note: main means chief or most important
a stream is a current of water

explanation.surface: A jazz style is described as both leading and up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream jazz names the swing-based style between traditional jazz and bebop, so it is a particular jazz idiom.

clue.text: Lawman with newly formed Tea Party

indicators.note: newly formed means made up afresh, so the letters of Tea Party are rearranged

explanation.surface: A law officer joins the newly founded Tea Party movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a Wild West marshal famed for the gunfight at the OK Corral, an example of a lawman.

clue.text: Slander a small individual I introduced

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the letter I goes inside the word for individual

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Someone slanders a short person who was introduced to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging, often false, remark about someone, much the same as a slander.

clue.text: Date long depression

parts.note: to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A date brings a lasting low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch is a long narrow trench, a depression in the ground.

clue.text: Ring in private

definitions.meaning: on an archery or shooting target, the ring next to the bullseye is called by this name
inward or personal, as in one's hidden thoughts and feelings

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a target ring nearest the centre and also means personal or hidden, as in a secret inward life.

clue.text: Strike front of ship, with 50 on vessel

parts.note: to punch is to strike
the bow is the front of a ship
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the bows of a ship that has fifty aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like part of the shipping scene, but it is the definition: a bowl is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbowl is a large bowl for serving punch, a kind of container or vessel.

clue.text: Salesman René, in tune, possibly, with Rex, a middleman

indicators.note: in tells us the salesman and the name go inside the reworked word
possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters of tune are rearranged

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a salesman
taken as written, the French name
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A salesman called René, musically in tune, works alongside Rex as an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas break the surface into wordplay pieces; 'middleman' reflects an older meaning of the word, a contractor or go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense this word meant a go-between or contractor who acts as an intermediary in business dealings.

clue.text: Plane crashed in Asian country

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so the letters of plane are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft came down in an Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan nation in South Asia, an example of an Asian country.

clue.text: In favour of male cast

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for

explanation.surface: Supporting an all-male cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads like a set of actors, but it is a mould for shaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a shape or mould, and a form is likewise a mould into which something is shaped.

clue.text: Disorder in Times Square

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words that follow it

explanation.surface: There is chaos in New York's Times Square.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of untidiness or confusion, a synonym for disorder.

clue.text: Last of such fish in list

indicators.note: last of means take the final letter of the next word

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: The last fish of this kind on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a roster, but it is the verb for a ship leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To heel is to lean over to one side, as a boat does, which is also what listing means.

clue.text: Trendy school and capital variety theatre

parts.note: hip means fashionable or trendy
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A fashionable school and a capital city have a variety theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a group of sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Many British music halls, such as the London venue of that name, were called this, so it means a variety theatre.

clue.text: Obscure English coin

parts.note: to dim is to obscure or darken

explanation.surface: An obscure old English coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English coin' suggests a British piece, but English only gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent piece, an example of a coin.

clue.text: Cruel men tortured American fictional character

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters of cruel men are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cruel men tortured an American storybook figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel Chandler Harris created this old storyteller narrator of the Br'er Rabbit tales, a character of fiction.
